messages:
jess-customer: Hey team — customer reporting streaming responses from our hosted API get cut off after ~8–12s. Client sees partial JSON/event and then the connection closes. Reconnect sometimes returns 401. Running behind Cloudflare + NLB.
sara-support: Thanks Jess. Can you paste a minimal repro and the response headers from the client side? Any pattern on when it cuts off (idle, heavy load)?
jess-customer: Repro curl we used:

```
curl -N -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' \
  -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' \
  'https://api.redwood.prod/v1/stream?model=open-52k' 
```
Observed output looks like this (truncated):

```
event: message
data: {"id":"r1","chunk":"Hello, this is a re"}

# then silent for a few secs, then connection resets, client shows HTTP/1.1 200 followed by socket close
```
Headers captured by client just before close:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
content-type: text/event-stream
transfer-encoding: chunked
x-cache: MISS from cloudflare
cf-ray: 78a1:abcd:us-east
x-nlb-id: nj-12345
```
Also saw occasional `401` on immediate reconnects (token is short-lived).
eli-eng: Sounds like proxy idle windowing / buffer coalescing. Cloudflare + NLB/TCP passthrough can coalesce small chunks into larger packets, then LB idle probes can half-close and trigger resets. 401 on reconnect indicates token rotation/expiry edge.
ryan-sre: Common stack notes:
- ALB/NLB default idle timeouts are low (60s). Cloudflare may proxy upstream and collapse chunks when upstream uses HTTP/1.1 vs HTTP/2.
- Some NGiNX/Envoy configs enable proxy buffering which will aggregate small SSE chunks.
min-ml: Can we get request id + origin instance logs? If the runtime is doing small-chunk flushes (every token), but the upstream proxies buffer, we see delays then an abrupt FIN.
sara-support: Jess — a few quick mitigations to try on customer side while we investigate:
- Add a 15s heartbeat comment to the SSE stream (send ":\n\n" periodically) to keep some activity through proxies.
- Ensure Authorization tokens used on reconnect are valid or issue refresh on 401.
- If using Cloudflare, try toggling HTTP/2 -> HTTP/1.1 to see if it changes chunking behavior.
Code snippet for heartbeat (node):

```
res.write(': heartbeat\n\n'); // comment keeps SSE alive
setInterval(() => res.write(': h\n\n'), 15000);
```
eli-eng: Server/runtime mitigations we can do:
- Ensure we flush stdout/network buffers after every SSE chunk (runtime already flushes, but kernel-level coalescing may still combine).
- Add `Connection: keep-alive` + small heartbeat tokens.
- Provide a reconnect-friendly envelope: include a resume token and byte/offset so clients can request resume rather than full replay.
ryan-sre: Platform ops suggestions for proxys:
- For ALB: increase idle timeout to 350s for streaming routes.
- For NLB/TCP passthrough: ensure TCP keepalives are enabled and tuned on the client and origin.
- For Cloudflare: `origin_request_buffering off` and disable `proxy_buffering` on any intermediate nginx. Consider `chunked_transfer_encoding on; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Connection '';` in nginx.
jess-customer: We tried a simple heartbeat and it reduced disconnects, but still see occasional early truncation when traffic is high and after long idle periods. The 401s were because their auth tokens rotate every 30s — reconnect logic was naive.
min-ml: That matches: idle window + sudden rehydrate after buffering. When the buffer flushes, kernel may coalesce and if LB has half-closed the connection, the flush triggers a RST. We should capture TCP-level traces next.
sara-support: Action items:
- Jess: ask customer to implement heartbeat + fix reconnect to refresh token on 401s (ETA: today).
- Ryan: check edge LB idle settings for the customer’s region + verify TCP keepalive defaults (ETA: 4h).
- Eli/min: we’ll instrument runtime to emit periodic keepalive comments when streaming long responses and add resume-token header (follow-up RFC) (ETA: 3d).
deploybot: Created ticket #INFR-8932 assigned to eng-runtime and sre with logs from customer: https://redwood-internal/tickets/INFR-8932
eli-eng: One-off debug steps we want from customer if they can run them:
1) `tcpdump -w sse-trace.pcap tcp and host <origin-ip>` while reproducing.
2) curl with `--http1.1 -v` and `--no-keepalive` to compare behaviour.
3) capture reconnect Authorization header to see token value/age.
jess-customer: I'll email the customer the repro commands and ask for pcaps + timestamp. Thanks — will update thread when they respond. :thumbsup:
sara-support: Thanks — marking as ongoing. If they can’t provide pcaps we’ll try to reproduce in staging with Cloudflare emulation and NLB config.
